dk profile arm: RaggedAllToAllDeviceKernelImpl busy ~3.3 s/step (384 launches x 8.5 ms) vs one-shot transport 1.77; ~1.9x in-kernel, all on the critical path; line-rate is ~30 ms so both kernels are latency/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound

t1024 occupancy patch NULL: 19.34 == unpatched dk band; per-SM in-flight bytes not the limit. i19 trace: one-shot copy 4.85 ms/launch (~660 GB/s, line rate), its NCCL barrier kernels only 0.12 ms; dk 8.52 ms (~380 GB/s). Next: per-peer CTA parallelism (g4x256)
g4x256 grid patch: 21.02, +1.65 over stock dk 19.37; per-peer CTA parallelism confirmed as the dk bottleneck; gap to one-shot 22.8 now 1.8; next g8x128
g8x128: 21.69; CTA-parallelism axis still climbing (19.37/21.02/21.69 at 1x/4x/8x); gap to one-shot 1.1; next g16x128 = one CTA per update, end of axis

g16x128 (one CTA per update): 21.11, REGRESSION vs g8x128 21.69 -- CTA-parallelism axis peaks at 8x/1024 threads-per-SM; residual +2.3 ms/launch vs one-shot; next: multimem (NVLS) LSA barriers on the g8x128 geometry

g8x128mm multimem LSA barrier: ILLEGAL_ADDRESS before step 0 -- comm.lsaMultimem not provisioned by XLA host-side requirements, needs real host wiring not a ctor flag; unicast-storm hypothesis also weakened (8x more CTAs improved perf)

g8x128 profile: dk kernel 4.56 ms/launch == one-shot 4.85 (PER-LAUNCH PARITY); residual gap is 2x a2a ops/step (576 vs 288, ~12 distinct ops/layer vs 8) -- backward RECOMPUTES forward transport under symbuf registration; +288 launches x 4.56 ms = 1.3 s/step == the 1.1 MFU gap

one-shot (WithNccl barrier) on main vintage: ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at startup -- MultiGpuBarrierWithNcclKernel arrays are kMaxPeers=32-sized with NO count check at 64 ranks; one-shot on unpatched main dead either path, kMaxPeers patch required

one-shot on kmax128-only MAIN wheel: 22.77 == wheel one-shot 22.78 -- doubling is NOT vintage-wide, it follows the dk flag (operand registration blocks the backward-recompute elision the output-only one-shot gets); one-shot needs exactly ONE upstream line (kMaxPeers) on main

i25/i27 REINTERPRETED: the 2x launch count is an op SPLIT under scoped registration (both transports, half payload each), not backward recompute -- one-shot busy unchanged (576x2.48=1.43 vs 288x4.85=1.40 s/step); dk at equal payload is 4.56 vs 2.48 ms = ~1.8x per byte, which IS the residual 1.1 MFU
